title: The Bathtubs or the Boiler Room

sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球知名的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境方面最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州及全球各地合作创新，寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该大学旨在提升所有生命生活质量使命的一部分。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 请登录 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: I have this habit of walking into any door that's unlocked,
sentences.zh: 我有顺手推开任何没锁的门的习惯，

sentences.en: and it actually does me well here in the Capitol because you start poking around and going into doors and you find the coolest things.
sentences.zh: 这在国会大厦里对我的工作很有帮助，因为你开始四处摸索、推开一扇扇门时，总能发现最酷的事情。

sentences.en: You have to appreciate the moxie of someone who can wander around a federal building, open up a random door, and announce to whoever's on the other side.
sentences.zh: 你不得不佩服这种人，能在一个联邦大楼里四处闲逛，随手推开一扇门，然后对里面的人说上一句。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrea Seabrook with NPR.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是NPR的安德烈亚·西布鲁克。

sentences.en: If you didn't catch that, that's NPR congressional correspondent Andrea Seabrook.
sentences.zh: 如果你没听清，那是NPR的国会记者安德烈亚·西布鲁克。

sentences.en: I'm a reporter.
sentences.zh: 我是一名记者。

sentences.en: We're poking around, looking at secret things in the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 我们在四处摸索，看看国会大厦里那些秘密的地方。

sentences.en: I am so in love with Andrea Seabrook right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在简直爱死安德烈亚·西布鲁克了。

sentences.en: The woman on the other side of the door tells Andrea that she needs to leave and that walking into random doors in the basement of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 门里边的那个女人告诉安德烈亚她必须离开，并说在美国国会大厦的地下室里随手开门

sentences.en: Capitol building is not what she's supposed to be doing.
sentences.zh: 可不是她该做的事。

sentences.en: And that's 99% Invisible's own Sam Greenspan.
sentences.zh: 那是《99%隐形》自己的萨姆·格林斯潘。

sentences.en: He went with Andrea to the Capitol building.
sentences.zh: 他和安德烈亚一起去了国会大厦。

sentences.en: I'm so jealous of him right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在可嫉妒他了。

sentences.en: That's not what we're supposed to be doing.
sentences.zh: 那可不是我们该做的事。

sentences.en: That doesn't deter you, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这并没有吓退你。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Are you kidding?
sentences.zh: 开什么玩笑？

sentences.en: I don't care what they think I'm supposed to be doing.
sentences.zh: 我才不管他们觉得我该做什么呢。

sentences.en: I'm here to cover the United States Capitol.
sentences.zh: 我是来报道美国国会大厦的。

sentences.en: And frankly, I see this as part of it.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我觉得这也是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Even if you try to set aside its role as the hub of Western democracy, the Capitol building itself, just the building, is an overwhelming structure.
sentences.zh: 抛开它作为西方民主中心的枢纽角色不谈，国会大厦本身，单单是这座建筑，就是一个气势磅礴的庞然大物。

sentences.en: There are 6,000 people who work in this complex.
sentences.zh: 这个建筑群里有6000名工作人员。

sentences.en: That's including the staffers, though.
sentences.zh: 不过这是算上幕僚的。

sentences.en: Not including the politicians.
sentences.zh: 不算那些政客。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a huge city.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它就像一座巨大的城市。

sentences.en: And it has one function, if you can call it a function, and that is running the legislative branch, the government.
sentences.zh: 它只有一个功能，如果你能称之为功能的话，那就是运转政府的立法部门。

sentences.en: Both, you know, writing the bills and cleaning the toilets.
sentences.zh: 不管是起草法案，还是清洗马桶，你知道的。

sentences.en: As if we could tell the difference.
sentences.zh: 就好像我们能分清它们的区别一样。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说的对吧？

sentences.en: The Capitol is known for its grandeur.
sentences.zh: 国会大厦以其宏伟壮丽而闻名。

sentences.en: The rotunda, the statuary hall, the crypt, the marble staircases.
sentences.zh: 圆形大厅、雕像大厅、地下室、大理石楼梯。

sentences.en: This place is unbelievably ornamental.
sentences.zh: 这个地方有着难以置信的丰富装饰。

sentences.en: The walls upstairs have gorgeous friezes, you know, with birds and squirrels and gorgeous, gorgeous, lilting, beautiful paintwork.
sentences.zh: 楼上的墙壁上有华丽的带饰，画着鸟儿和松鼠，还有极其华丽、轻快、美丽的彩绘。

sentences.en: And that's all the stuff we're supposed to see.
sentences.zh: 而这些都是我们本就该看到的东西。

sentences.en: But when you're an inveterate doorknob turner and snoop like Andrea Seabrook, you also get to know the Capitol below the surface.
sentences.zh: 但当你像安德烈亚·西布鲁克那样，是一个无可救药的门把手狂热者和搜奇者时，你也能见识到地面之下的国会大厦。

sentences.en: Literally, the basement.
sentences.zh: 字面意思上的地下室。

sentences.en: Down here, there's a whole bunch of engineers, you know, like HVAC engineers in blue uniforms that say, like, you know, Joe on them.
sentences.zh: 在这里，有一大群工程师，比如暖通空调工程师，穿着蓝色制服，上面印着诸如乔之类名字。

sentences.en: The purpose of the building, the business of government trickles down to these lower levels.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑的用途、政府的事务一点点渗透到了这些底层。

sentences.en: The members of the House, Republican caucus and sometimes the Democrats, meet in the basement for their sort of closed door secret strategy sessions.
sentences.zh: 众议院议员们，共和党党团有时还有民主党人，会聚集在地下室举行某种闭门秘密战略会议。

sentences.en: And it's a really good place to, excuse me, it's a really good place to get kind of a tip from members that you know about what's going on.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的地方，不好意思，这真是个打听消息的好地方，能从你熟悉的议员那里打听到正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: But the main reason we're here is to see a little bit of the architectural grandeur that has trickled down here, too.
sentences.zh: 但我们来这里的核心原因，是想看看那些也渗透到这里的建筑壮丽之美。

sentences.en: Oh, it says, please check in with the engineers, which I think they'll do, just, you know.
sentences.zh: 哦，上面写着，请先向工程师登记，我想他们会照做的，你知道的。

sentences.en: One thing that's cool is, um, I'll just show it to you.
sentences.zh: 有意思的是，嗯，我这就带你看看。

sentences.en: Andrea is leading me through the serpentine route of alleys and doorways and...
sentences.zh: 安德烈亚正带着我穿过弯弯曲曲的小巷和门廊，还有……

sentences.en: Really in the, uh, what?
sentences.zh: 真的在，呃，什么？

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪。

sentences.en: Here we are.
sentences.zh: 我们到了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊艳了。

sentences.en: And then there are these bathtubs.
sentences.zh: 然后还有这些浴缸。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: They're these beautiful marble bathtubs with marble steps that lead up to them and brass fittings.
sentences.zh: 这些是精美的大理石浴缸，配有通往浴缸的大理石台阶和黄铜配件。

sentences.en: And they're deep, beautiful bathtubs.
sentences.zh: 而且它们是深邃、美丽的浴缸。

sentences.en: Just to describe it a little bit, it's, it's sort of a white ivory marble that has this luster.
sentences.zh: 稍微描述一下的话，这是一种象牙白色的大理石，带有这种独特的光泽。

sentences.en: It reminds me of the Venus de Milo or something.
sentences.zh: 让我想起了米洛斯的维纳斯之类的雕像。

sentences.en: It shines, it glows a little bit, and it's got very faint black veins in it.
sentences.zh: 它闪闪发光，散发着微弱的光芒，上面还有非常淡的黑色纹理。

sentences.en: And it's just gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 简直美极了。

sentences.en: The curves in it are so gentle and continuous.
sentences.zh: 上面的曲线是那么柔和且连贯。

sentences.en: But for all the grandeur the tubs possess, the room itself is the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 但尽管这些浴缸拥有种种宏伟气派，房间本身却与其截然相反。

sentences.en: This place was supposed to cool off senators.
sentences.zh: 这个地方曾经是用来给参议员们降温的。

sentences.en: Now it cools and heats the entire Capitol building.
sentences.zh: 现在它为整座国会大厦提供冷暖气。

sentences.en: There's big HVAC equipment and computer servers and large steel cabinets containing God knows what.
sentences.zh: 这里有大型暖通空调设备、计算机服务器以及装着天知道什么东西的大型钢制机柜。

sentences.en: Even though the bathtubs, along with the sink and toilet, were here first, they're the ones that seem out of place.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些浴缸以及洗手盆和马桶是最早出现在这里的，但它们反倒成了最显格格不入的东西。

sentences.en: The bathtubs were installed around 1860, during the expansion of the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 这些浴缸大约在1860年国会大厦扩建期间安装。

sentences.en: D.C.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿特区

sentences.en: is known for its swampy summers, and legend has it that senators could be banished from the chamber if they were too smelly.
sentences.zh: 以闷热的夏天闻名，传说如果参议员们身上气味太难闻，就会被逐出议事厅。

sentences.en: It still reeks, but yeah, back then it was less figurative.
sentences.zh: 现在那里依然臭气熏天，不过好吧，当年可不是比喻。

sentences.en: And most people at the time, even politicians, they didn't have indoor plumbing at home.
sentences.zh: 而且当时大多数人，甚至包括政客，家里都没有室内上下水设施。

sentences.en: So Congress needed a place where the politicians could go and wash up.
sentences.zh: 所以国会需要一个地方，让政客们能去那里梳洗一番。

sentences.en: Andrea reads from an informational card beside the tub.
sentences.zh: 安德烈亚宣读着浴缸旁边的说明卡。

sentences.en: Okay, here we go.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们来看看。

sentences.en: Each bathtub, and I am standing in one right now, was carved in Italy from a single block of Carrara marble.
sentences.zh: 每个浴缸——我此刻正站在其中一个里面——都是在意大利由一整块卡拉拉大理石雕刻而成的。

sentences.en: Three bathtubs were shipped from Genoa, Italy in July 1859 and reached Baltimore in November of that year.
sentences.zh: 1859年7月，三个浴缸从意大利热那亚装船运出，并于当年11月抵达巴尔的摩。

sentences.en: July to November.
sentences.zh: 从7月到11月。

sentences.en: The other three were shipped from Leghorn, Italy in September of 1859 and arrived in New York in January of 1860.
sentences.zh: 另外三个于1859年9月从意大利里窝那发货，并于1860年1月抵达纽约。

sentences.en: The precise dates of the bathtub's arrival and installation at the Capitol are uncertain,
sentences.zh: 这些浴缸抵达并安装在国会大厦的具体日期尚不确定，

sentences.en: but the Senate Bathing Room is known to have been in operation as of February 23rd, 1860.
sentences.zh: 但已知参议院浴室从1860年2月23日起就已经投入使用了。

sentences.en: Each of the six tubs cost $90 in 1860, which is around $2,500 apiece today.
sentences.zh: 在1860年，这六个浴缸每个造价90美元，折合当今每个约合2500美元。

sentences.en: And that was just to buy the tubs.
sentences.zh: 而且这还只是购买浴缸的费用。

sentences.en: You got to figure it was still more to ship them from Italy, receive them at the Port of Baltimore,
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，把它们从意大利海运过来、在巴尔的摩港接收、

sentences.en: transport them to Capitol Hill, and then you had to build a bathing facility suitable to a senator.
sentences.zh: 运到国会山，还要建造一个配得上参议员身份的沐浴设施，还需要花更多的钱。

sentences.en: They had oakwood paneling.
sentences.zh: 它们拥有橡木镶板。

sentences.en: Plaster cornices.
sentences.zh: 石膏檐口。

sentences.en: Minton tile.
sentences.zh: 明顿瓷砖。

sentences.en: Egg and dart molding.
sentences.zh: 蛋箭饰线条。

sentences.en: Of the six original tubs, only two are left.
sentences.zh: 在原本的六个浴缸中，只剩下两个了。

sentences.en: And one has a piece of plywood over it that props up some padlocked steel mystery box.
sentences.zh: 其中一个上面盖着一块胶合板，上面支撑着一个带锁的神秘钢制盒子。

sentences.en: The other was decommissioned years ago.
sentences.zh: 另一个在多年前就已经退役了。

sentences.en: This place is a total collision of eras, not just old versus new.
sentences.zh: 这个地方简直是各个时代的碰撞，绝不仅仅是新旧之别。

sentences.en: And I know that just a little bit ago, we were considering the Capitol building as just a building.
sentences.zh: 我知道就在刚才，我们还把国会大厦仅仅看作是一座建筑。

sentences.en: It's impossible to look at this room and not see a metaphorical debate right here in the basement.
sentences.zh: 但看着这个房间，你不可能不在地下室里看到一场隐喻性的辩论。

sentences.en: We are having this great debate in our country, whether you're in the Tea Party or the Occupy movement,
sentences.zh: 我们国家正在进行一场大辩论，无论你是属于茶党还是占领运动，

sentences.en: both share the same concern about who the government is for.
sentences.zh: 双方都对政府究竟是为谁服务有着同样的担忧。

sentences.en: And I think the politicians have tried really hard to make it look as if the government is for the people
sentences.zh: 我想政客们一直非常努力地营造出这样一种假象：政府是为人民服务的，

sentences.en: and not for the gorgeously appointed bathers of the world.
sentences.zh: 而不是为世界上那些享受豪华沐浴的人服务的。

sentences.en: For example, when Newt Gingrich took over the House speakership in 1995,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，当纽特·金里奇在1995年接任众议院议长时，

sentences.en: after, you know, a giant sweep of the 94 elections,
sentences.zh: 在经历94年选举的巨大横扫之后，

sentences.en: he found that there were buckets of ice still being delivered to every single member of Congress's office,
sentences.zh: 他发现仍然有成桶的冰块被送到每一位国会议员的办公室，

sentences.en: even though they all had refrigerators with ice makers.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们所有人其实都拥有带制冰机的冰箱。

sentences.en: It was back from the time when you had to buy ice separately.
sentences.zh: 那是必须单独购买冰块的那个年代遗留产物。

sentences.en: And so they sort of shut down all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把这些东西全关停了。

sentences.en: At the same time, they got rid of the House historian.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们解散了众议院历史学家办公室。

sentences.en: They defunded all of these things they thought of as luxuries.
sentences.zh: 他们削减了所有被他们认为是奢侈品的预算。

sentences.en: And they got rid of a lot of the funding for saving things like this.
sentences.zh: 他们取消了用于保护此类事物的许多资金支持。

sentences.en: As Andrea puts it, the spending versus austerity question
sentences.zh: 正如安德烈亚所说，花钱还是紧缩的问题，

sentences.en: is really just the modern form of the quintessential American question of government.
sentences.zh: 其实不过是美国关于政府本质这一经典问题的现代形式。

sentences.en: Which is, how much government should exist?
sentences.zh: 也就是，政府究竟该存在多少？

sentences.en: What is it there to do?
sentences.zh: 它的职责到底是什么？

sentences.en: And at one point, about 140 some odd years ago,
sentences.zh: 曾经在140多年前的某个时期，

sentences.en: there was this idea of the government being an important institution,
sentences.zh: 人们曾认为政府是一个重要的机构，

sentences.en: one that would have gorgeously appointed baths.
sentences.zh: 一个会拥有豪华装修浴室的机构。

sentences.en: And now, we're sitting in a boiler room,
sentences.zh: 而现在，我们坐在一个锅炉房里，

sentences.en: and the beautiful Minton tile has been painted over with industrial gray paint,
sentences.zh: 美丽明顿瓷砖被刷上了工业灰色油漆，

sentences.en: and the walls are kind of dirty, and it's loud,
sentences.zh: 墙壁有点脏，而且很吵闹，

sentences.en: and there's no way to pay homage to it anymore.
sentences.zh: 再也没有办法向它致敬了。

sentences.en: It's tucked in a corner and dirty,
sentences.zh: 它被塞在角落里，脏兮兮的，

sentences.en: and there's a roach trap on the floor.
sentences.zh: 地板上还有一个蟑螂屋。

sentences.en: How gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 多么华丽啊。

sentences.en: See how the marble kind of sparkles a little bit?
sentences.zh: 看大理石是怎么隐隐闪光的？

sentences.en: If it's a little bit clean, look close to you.
sentences.zh: 如果稍微清理一下，仔细看看。

sentences.en: You see this sort of luster?
sentences.zh: 你看到这种光泽了吗？

sentences.en: I don't think there's any modern political persuasion
sentences.zh: 我想现在没有任何一个政治派别

sentences.en: that would advocate for the installation of luxurious
sentences.zh: 会主张为参议员安装豪华的

sentences.en: $3,000 marble bathtubs for senators.
sentences.zh: 价值3000美元的大理石浴缸。

sentences.en: As lovely as they may be.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们可能很可爱。

sentences.en: The bathtubs, not the senators.
sentences.zh: 我是说浴缸，不是参议员。

sentences.en: But if the ornate marble bathtubs are already there,
sentences.zh: 但如果这些华丽的大理石浴缸已经在那里了，

sentences.en: they were installed 150 years ago,
sentences.zh: 它们是150年前安装的，

sentences.en: what do you do with them?
sentences.zh: 你该拿它们怎么办？

sentences.en: What represents the people now?
sentences.zh: 现在又有什么能代表人民呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it's interesting that it's still preserved,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它能被保存下来很有趣，

sentences.en: but it's likely not going to be restored.
sentences.zh: 但它大概不会被修复了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Not unless we had some resurgence in respect for our government.
sentences.zh: 除非我们对政府的敬意有所复苏。

sentences.en: Can you imagine the people wanting to pay?
sentences.zh: 你能想象人们愿意花钱吗？

sentences.en: Even if it was only, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 哪怕只有，我不知道，

sentences.en: give it $500,000, just to be crazy,
sentences.zh: 哪怕拿出50万美元，就当是疯了一回，

sentences.en: just to restore this area.
sentences.zh: 仅仅为了修复这个区域。

sentences.en: It may be a lot more than that, actually,
sentences.zh: 说实话，考虑到你得搬走多少东西，实际花费可能会远远超过这个数字。

sentences.en: come to think of how much you'd have to move.
sentences.zh: 不过，我不知道。

sentences.en: But, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 你想去开几扇门吗？

sentences.en: You want to go open some doors?
sentences.zh: 好啊。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 走吧。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Sam Greenspan,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由山姆·格林斯潘制作，

sentences.en: who I'm so jealous of, and he's totally fired.
